sources.entry: OpnForm - Beautiful form builder. (Demo, Source Code) AGPL-3.0 PHP/Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: OpnForm is an open-source, AGPL-3.0 form builder offered as a managed cloud service or self-hosted via Docker, PHP and Node.js.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a no-code form builder with unlimited forms and submissions, many input types (text, date, URL, file uploads), and embedding in other sites. It lists email notifications, integrations (Slack, Webhooks, Discord), form logic and customization, captcha protection, and form analytics. A remote MCP server lets AI agents create and preview private form drafts, with OAuth for workspace-aware management and read-only submission search, statistics and exports. Spreadsheet exports keep numeric zeros, leading-zero identifiers and Unicode. PDF templates can map fields to zones on a PDF. Most of the README is developer-focused notes on performance, dependency security, a Codex worktree dev setup, and bundle size checks rather than end-user setup.
use_cases: collect file uploads through a form
send form submission notifications to Slack or Discord
embed a form on a website
self-host a form builder instead of using a SaaS
how_to_run: For self-hosted installs, follow the Deployment Guides linked from the README (not reproduced in the README itself).
For local development, use the minimal Docker-based setup described in the Docker Development Guide.
notable: Ships a remote MCP server and plugin package so AI agents can create form drafts without logging in
Dual-licensed: core under AGPLv3, with Enterprise features under api/app/Enterprise/ under a proprietary license
Managed cloud service is the primary path; self-hosting is documented through separate deployment guides
Includes a Codex worktree dev environment with seeded data and a local admin account
caveats: Enterprise Edition features under api/app/Enterprise/ are proprietary, not AGPL
README points to external guides for self-hosted deployment; it does not give full install steps
Specific runtime requirements apply: PHP 8.3 or 8.4 and Node 22/24 or newer
